approved: Currency (Restrictions on the Use of Cash) Bill 2019

The majority voted against an [amendment](https://www.openaustralia.org.au/debates/?id=2019-10-24.13.1) to the usual second reading motion, which is that the bill be read for a [second time](https://www.peo.gov.au/understand-our-parliament/how-parliament-works/bills-and-laws/making-a-law-in-the-australian-parliament/) (parliamentary jargon for agreeing with the main idea of the bill). The amendment was introduced by Whitlam MP [Stephen Jones](https://theyvoteforyou.org.au/people/representatives/whitlam/stephen_jones) (Labor). ### Amendment text > *That all words after "That" be omitted with a view to substituting the following words:* > > *"whilst not declining to give the bill a second reading, the House:* > > *(1) recognises the importance of cash for conducting transactions around Australia; and* > > *(2) notes the concerns that have arisen in some parts of the community about the bill, in the context of the stagnating Australian economy under the Coalition Government".*

The speaker moved an amendment to the Currency (Restrictions on the Use of Cash) Bill 2019, which would establish a $10,000 cash payment limit from 1 January 2020 with penalties of up to $25,000 or two years imprisonment, and argued that Labor would not oppose the bill in the House but would seek rigorous Senate scrutiny due to community concerns, while criticising the Coalition government's economic management for stagnant wages, low growth, and declining household incomes.

The speaker opposed the Currency (Restrictions on the Use of Cash) Bill 2019, arguing it is unnecessary and distracts from weak enforcement of existing anti-money laundering laws, and highlighted failures by AUSTRAC, VCGLR, VicPol, Border Force, ASIC, and ASX, using Crown casino money laundering as a case study.

The speaker opposed the Currency (Restrictions on the Use of Cash) Bill 2019, arguing it restricts personal freedom, disadvantages rural and older Australians due to bank branch closures, and is hypocritical given government inaction on money laundering at Crown casino and the Commonwealth Bank's failure to report over 53,000 transactions. The bill imposes a strict liability offence for cash transactions over $10,000, and the speaker noted AUSTRAC's $100 million budget and specific bank closures in Mayo (ANZ Goolwa, ANZ Lobethal, Commonwealth Bank Stirling and Strathalbyn).
